Compare two versions of a table by key

Source: R/compare.R
sv_compare.Rd

Compares two cuts of the same table row by row. Rows are matched on the key columns (NA matches NA) and reported as added (only in new), removed (only in old), changed (matched, with a different value in a column) or the same. A key that repeats in either version leaves all its rows, in both versions, out of every count and table; the summary reports it as a warning with up to 5 sample keys, the first in sorted order.

Usage

sv_compare(old, new, by = NULL)

Arguments

old, new

Data frames, duckdb tables or Arrow tables: the earlier and the later version. Unnamed tables are named by their expressions, as sideview() names them.

by

Names of the key columns, the same in both versions (1 to 20). NULL suggests a key: the first shared column (same name, similar values) with no repeated value in either version, else the shared columns together when their combinations are unique, else an error asks for the key. For a duckdb or Arrow table the suggestion reads the first 50 rows of each version.

Value

An object of class sv_compare: old_name, new_name, by, the row counts n_old, n_new, n_added, n_removed, n_changed, same, the repeated-key counts, per_column (changed rows per compared column), text (summary lines) and open (button labels), plus the tables added, removed and changed, and code.

Details

Compared columns are those in both versions with the same type kind, so an integer column equals a double column of the same values and a factor equals a character column. A column whose kind differs is listed in type_changed, not compared. Key columns are not compared. Equality is exact; NA and NaN in both versions are the same, and one of them against a value is a change. Key columns of differing kinds are matched as text.

The changed table has the key columns, then column, old and new (the values as text, missing values NA), ordered by key and then by the column's position in new.

When either version is a duckdb or Arrow table, both are compared on one duckdb connection and nothing is collected: the counts come from queries, and added, removed and changed are lazy duckdb tables (in no particular order). Number text can then differ from R's ("100000" for "1e+05").

Examples

cut1 <- data.frame(id = 1:4, sev = c("MILD", "MILD", "SEVERE", "MILD"))
cut2 <- data.frame(id = 2:5, sev = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE", "MILD"))
sv_compare(cut1, cut2, by = "id")
#> cut1 -> cut2, key id
#> Rows:    4 -> 4   added 1 · removed 1 · changed 2 · same 1
#> Columns: added none · removed none · type changed none
#> Changed values by column:  sev 2
#> added: 1 row
#> removed: 1 row
#> changed values: 2
